notes: The circuit images (IMG04, IMG05, IMG07) were not provided, so the LED wiring is inferred from the sketch: LED_1 on pin 3, LED_2 on pin 4. Each LED has a series resistor, and each cathode goes to a GND rail.
Breadboard hole positions are my assumption: the images were not available, so the exact holes and the 220 ohm resistor value are guesses.
The tutorial says 'Arduino MKR family board' without naming one. I used arduino-mkr-1000 as a stand-in, because its ports include 1-4, GND, VCC and 5V.

The MKR board's pins plug into the shield's female headers. The LED jumper wires are attached to the board's own pins 3, 4 and GND, which are electrically the same as the shield's pass-through sockets.

Relays are wired internally to pins 1 and 2. The shield's high-power terminals (R1/R2 NO, COM, NC) are modelled as ports. The tutorial's high-power example (24V supply plus a 24V lamp on the NC contact) was only described as an image and has no catalogue part, so I left it out. The screw terminals and the NC/NO/COM contacts are left unconnected.
The shield's low-power logic (relay coils, driver, flyback diodes, A1-A4 solder jumpers) is internal to the shield and not modelled as separate parts. The proto area is unused.
The Arduino IDE, the USB cable and the code are not physical parts in the build graph.
